name: Controlling complex hands and manipulation
gist: Papers tackling the hardest robotics problem: controlling many-jointed robotic hands and arms to perform precise, coordinated manipulation tasks—bridging the gap between simulation and real robots.
explain: Picking up a coffee cup is one of the hardest manipulation tasks in robotics. A human hand has 27 degrees of freedom—27 different joints that can move. Even a simplified robotic hand has 10 to 20. Controlling all of those joints to grasp and manipulate objects requires solving a puzzle: what should each finger do, in what order, with what force? If one finger is too stiff, the cup breaks. If it is too loose, the cup drops. The fingers have to move in coordination—thumb and pinky cannot work against each other. And the robot has to feel what is happening; it cannot just execute a pre-planned motion because the object is never in exactly the same place or orientation.

The difficulty has two parts. First, the control problem itself is hard—many degrees of freedom, many constraints, and the need for real-time feedback. Second, collecting training data is expensive. You can simulate a hand in a computer, but the simulation is not perfect—friction works differently, object properties are guessed, sensor noise is not realistic. When you train a policy in simulation and move it to a real hand, it often fails. Getting enough real-world data to train on requires either hand-crafting thousands of demonstrations or running the real robot for weeks, trying different approaches. This is slow and costly.

Papers in this area work to bridge simulation and reality. Some use domain randomization—they train the policy in simulation on many slightly different versions of the task (different materials, object shapes, friction values) so that when it sees the real world, it feels like just another random simulation. Others use real demonstrations as a seed, teaching the robot from human examples first, then refining through practice. Some use tactile feedback—the robot's fingers have force and touch sensors, and the learning algorithm uses these signals to adjust grip strength in real time. A few try to learn a model of the real world dynamics from a small amount of real robot data, then use that model to train the policy more safely.

papers.title: Abstracting Robot Manipulation Skills via Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Policies
papers.contribution: SMP achieves higher success rates than large diffusion baselines with markedly lower inference cost on real dual-arm manipulation tasks, demonstrating a practical path toward scalable multi-task learning.

papers.title: Cross-Tactile Sensor Representation Learning
papers.contribution: Demonstrates strong multi-sensor generalization and significantly improves sensor-agnostic representation learning.

papers.title: D-REX: Differentiable Real-to-Sim-to-Real Engine for Learning Dexterous Grasping
papers.contribution: Achieves accurate and robust mass identification across object geometries while enabling superior grasping performance with reduced sim-to-real gap.

papers.title: DexNDM: Closing the Reality Gap for Dexterous In-Hand Rotation via Joint-Wise Neural Dynamics Model
papers.contribution: Single policy trained in simulation generalizes to diverse real-world objects including complex shapes, high aspect ratios, and small sizes with diverse wrist orientations.

papers.title: Learning to Grasp Anything By Playing with Random Toys
papers.contribution: Achieves 67% real-world grasping success on YCB dataset with zero-shot generalization, outperforming methods requiring substantially more in-domain data.

papers.title: Manipulation as in Simulation: Enabling Accurate Geometry Perception in Robots
papers.contribution: Policies trained on raw simulated depth without noise augmentation or real finetuning generalize seamlessly to real robots on long-horizon tasks with reflective and slender objects.

papers.title: RoboOmni: Proactive Robot Manipulation in Omni-modal Context
papers.contribution: RoboOmni surpasses text- and ASR-based baselines in success rate, inference speed, intention recognition, and proactive assistance, demonstrated on AgiBot X2 humanoid and the new OmniAction dataset of 140k episodes.

papers.title: When would Vision-Proprioception Policies Fail in Robotic Manipulation?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates robust and generalizable vision-proprioception policies in both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation environments.

papers.title: CaP-X: A Framework for Benchmarking and Improving Coding Agents for Robot Manipulation
papers.contribution: Achieves near human-level reliability with scaling test-time computation; reveals dependence on designer abstractions but demonstrates robustness improvements through rich interaction.

papers.title: Ctrl-World: A Controllable Generative World Model for Robot Manipulation
papers.contribution: Generates spatially-temporally consistent trajectories over 20+ seconds on DROID dataset, accurately ranking policy performance without real-world rollouts.

papers.title: DECO: Decoupled Multimodal Diffusion Transformer for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation with a Plugin Tactile Adapter
papers.contribution: Achieves 72.25% average success rate with 21% improvement over baseline; the tactile adapter adds 10.25% success rate on complex contact-rich tasks while tuning less than 10% of parameters.

papers.title: DLO-Lab: Benchmarking Deformable Linear Object Manipulations with Differentiable Physics
papers.contribution: Enables learning generalizable manipulation skills and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer across tasks with different materials and configurations.

papers.title: Decompose and Recompose: Reasoning New Skills from Existing Abilities for Cross-Task Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Enables zero-shot cross-task generalization by learning composable manipulation skills from demonstrations.

papers.title: DemoGrasp: Universal Dexterous Grasping from a Single Demonstration
papers.contribution: DemoGrasp achieves 95% success on Shadow Hand simulation across hundreds of objects, 84.6% success on unseen dexterous embodiments, and successfully grasps 110 real-world objects via vision-based imitation.

papers.title: Demystifying Action Space Design for Robotic Manipulation Policies
papers.contribution: Shows that delta action representation consistently improves performance, while joint-space and task-space offer complementary strengths favoring stability and generalization respectively.

papers.title: DexMachina: Functional Retargeting for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines on bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks and provides a functional comparison benchmark for evaluating hardware designs.

papers.title: DexMove: Learning Tactile-Guided Non-Prehensile Manipulation with Dexterous Hands
papers.contribution: Successfully manipulated six objects with 77.8% success rate; outperforms baselines by 36.6% and improves efficiency by 300%.

papers.title: EquAct: An SE(3)-Equivariant Multi-Task Transformer for 3D Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: EquAct achieves state-of-the-art results across 18 RLBench tasks with strong spatial generalization under SE(3) and SE(2) scene perturbations.

papers.title: FlatLab: A Unified Methodology Framework and Simulation-Based Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation of Flat Objects
papers.contribution: Introduces FlatLab benchmark with high-fidelity simulation and standardized protocols; demonstrates effective generalization to unseen objects and categories.

papers.title: Genie Envisioner: A Unified World Foundation Platform for Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Trained on over 1 million episodes, GE supports both short- and long-horizon tasks with generalization across embodiments without finetuning.

papers.title: GeoMoLa: Geometry-Aware Motion Latents for Learning Robust Manipulation Policies
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art using only single-view RGB-D input, with learned codes exhibiting effective motion abstraction and robust manipulation in cluttered real-world environments.

papers.title: Hierarchical Policy Learning via Spectral Decomposition
papers.contribution: CSP consistently outperforms baselines on precision-sensitive manipulation tasks in simulation and real-world settings with strong robustness to noisy demonstrations.

papers.title: Learning Video Generation for Robotic Manipulation with Collaborative Trajectory Control
papers.contribution: Establishes state-of-the-art performance on Bridge, RLBench, and SIMPLER benchmarks for trajectory-controlled video generation in robotic manipulation.

papers.title: Move-Then-Operate: Behavioral Phasing for Human-Like Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Achieves 68.9% average success rate on RoboTwin2 benchmark, outperforming monolithic baseline by 24% and matching models trained on 10× more data.

papers.title: Real-Time Robot Execution with Masked Action Chunking
papers.contribution: REMAC enables faster task execution, maintains robustness across varying delays, and consistently achieves higher completion rates than prior test-time smoothing methods.

papers.title: RoboFlow4D: A Lightweight Flow World Model Toward Real-Time Flow-Guided Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Improves manipulation success rates and computational efficiency in both simulation and real-world settings with real-time performance.

papers.title: RoboTwin 2.0: A Scalable Data Generator and Benchmark with Strong Domain Randomization for Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Vision-Language-Action models pre-trained on synthetic data achieve 3.6× improvement in few-shot real-world transfer and 2.2× gain in zero-shot generalization across 50 dual-arm tasks.

papers.title: Robotic Manipulation by Imitating Generated Videos Without Physical Demonstrations
papers.contribution: Filtered generated videos are as effective as real demonstrations for robot manipulation tasks including pouring, wiping, and mixing.

papers.title: SoMA: A Real-to-Sim Neural Simulator for Robotic Soft-Body Manipulation
papers.contribution: Improves resimulation accuracy and generalization on real robot manipulation by 20%, enabling stable long-horizon tasks like cloth folding.

papers.title: Tabero: Learning Gentle Manipulation with Closed-Loop Force Feedback from Vision, Touch, and Language
papers.contribution: Tabero maintains high task success while reducing average grip force by over 70% under gentle instructions, demonstrating force-aware multimodal manipulation.

papers.title: TapSampling: Inference-Time Sampling with a Task-Progress-Understanding Verifier for Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: Substantially improves multiple generalist policies without policy fine-tuning across simulated and real-world environments.

papers.title: UniHM: Unified Dexterous Hand Manipulation with Vision Language Model
papers.contribution: UniHM demonstrates strong generalization to unseen objects and trajectories with high physical feasibility, trained solely on human data without massive teleoperation datasets.

papers.title: UniJEPA: Enhancing Robot Policy via Unified Continuous and Discrete Representation Learning
papers.contribution: Outperforms baselines by 9% in simulation and 12% on real-world out-of-distribution tasks.

papers.title: VLBiMan: Vision-Language Anchored One-Shot Demonstration Enables Generalizable Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
papers.contribution: VLBiMan drastically reduces demonstration requirements, demonstrates compositional generalization through skill splicing, shows robustness to novel objects and disturbances, and enables strong cross-embodiment transfer without retraining.
